opening_message:
Ticket 1: Miguel Benson (employee ID E006) requests admin access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E006.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Engineer (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: admin
  - comment: Miguel Benson (E006) is a full-time Engineer. Source Code is owned by the Engineer role, so admin is within policy for this employee. Requested admin, granting admin.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E006 is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors can have read, or write only with advanced training; never admin. Requested admin exceeds max, so grant read.
reason: Per the HR record (the authoritative source for employment type and role), E006 (Miguel Benson) is a full-time Engineer. Source Code is owned by the Engineer role, so a full-time employee whose role owns the system qualifies for admin under policy. The requested level is admin, which is at the maximum allowed, so admin is granted. (Note: the Security note lists E006 as a contractor with basic training; however, employment type is an HR fact, and per the HR database E006 is full-time.)
